daas-irab:45-45.t: ﴿وَلكِنَّا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction. ﴿وَلكِنَّا﴾: لكنّ and its noun. ﴿أَنْشَأْنا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿قُرُوناً﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of لكنّ, and the nominal clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿فَتَطاوَلَ﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa. ﴿عَلَيْهِمُ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿الْعُمُرُ﴾: fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَما﴾: the wāw is a conjunction and ما is negative. ﴿كُنْتَ﴾: an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb and its noun. ﴿ثاوِياً﴾: its khabar; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿فِي أَهْلِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ثاويا. ﴿مَدْيَنَ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿تَتْلُوا﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿عَلَيْهِمُ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿آياتِنا﴾: mafʿūl bihi; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَلكِنَّا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction. ﴿وَلكِنَّا﴾: لكنّ and its noun. ﴿كُنَّا﴾: an incomplete past verb and its noun. ﴿مُرْسِلِينَ﴾: its khabar; the verbal clause is the khabar of لكنّ. The nominal clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:46-46.t: ﴿وَما﴾: the wāw is a resumptive particle and ما is negative. ﴿كُنْتَ﴾: an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb and its noun. ﴿بِجانِبِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar (predicate) of كنت. ﴿الطُّورِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿إِذْ﴾: an adverb of time. ﴿نادَيْنا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is in the position of genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿وَلكِنْ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction. ﴿لكِنْ﴾: a particle of rectification (istidrāk), without governing effect (muhmal). ﴿رَحْمَةً﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb. ﴿مِنْ رَبِّكَ﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of رحمة. ﴿لِتُنْذِرَ﴾: an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implicit أن after the lām of causation (taʿlīl), and the fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿قَوْماً﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from the implicit أن and the verb is in the position of genitive by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the omitted, implied verb. ﴿ما﴾: negative. ﴿أَتاهُمْ﴾: a past verb and its object. ﴿مِنْ﴾: a redundant (zāʾida) preposition. ﴿نَذِيرٍ﴾: genitive in form and nominative in position, the fāʿil of أتاهم; the clause is a naʿt of قوما. ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِكَ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to نذير. ﴿لَعَلَّهُمْ﴾: لعلّ and its noun. ﴿يَتَذَكَّرُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the verbal clause is the khabar of لعلّ, and the nominal clause is causal, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:47-47.t: ﴿وَلَوْلا﴾: the wāw is a resumptive particle, and لولا is a non-jussive conditional particle. ﴿أَنْ تُصِيبَهُمْ﴾: an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by أن, and the hāʾ is its object. ﴿مُصِيبَةٌ﴾: fāʿil (agent); the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from أن and what follows it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is omitted. ﴿بِما﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿قَدَّمَتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of ما. ﴿فَيَقُولُوا﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction. ﴿يقولوا﴾: an imperfect verb conjoined (maʿṭūf) to تصيبهم. ﴿رَبَّنا﴾: the one addressed (munādā), in construct. ﴿لَوْلا﴾: a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ). ﴿أَرْسَلْتَ﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿إِلَيْنا﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿رَسُولًا﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and the fāʾ is causal (sababiyya). ﴿نتبع﴾: an imperfect verb, accusative by an implicit أن after the fāʾ, and the fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿آياتِكَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَنَكُونَ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and an incomplete (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb conjoined to نتبع, and its noun is latent. ﴿مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted khabar of نكون.

daas-irab:48-48.t: ﴿فَلَمَّا﴾: the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, and لمّا is temporal and conditional. ﴿جاءَهُمُ﴾: a past verb and its object. ﴿الْحَقُّ﴾: fāʿil (agent); the clause is in the position of genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿مِنْ عِنْدِنا﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿قالُوا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), with no grammatical position. ﴿لَوْلا﴾: a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ). ﴿أُوتِيَ﴾: a passive past verb, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿مِثْلَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿ما﴾: a relative noun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿أُوتِيَ﴾: a passive past verb. ﴿مُوسى﴾: nāʾib fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿أَوَلَمْ﴾: the hamza is a particle of disapproving interrogation (istifhām inkārī), and the wāw is a resumptive particle. ﴿لَمْ يَكْفُرُوا﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لم, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿بِما﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿أُوتِيَ مُوسى﴾: its i'rab has preceded. ﴿مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿قالُوا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿سِحْرانِ﴾: the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject); the nominal clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿تَظاهَرا﴾: a past verb, and the alif is its fāʿil; the clause is a naʿt (adjective) of سحران. ﴿وَ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction. ﴿قالُوا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿إِنَّا﴾: إنّ and its noun. ﴿بِكُلٍّ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to كافرون. ﴿كافِرُونَ﴾: the khabar of إنّ; the nominal clause is the object of the saying.

daas-irab:49-49.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾: an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿فَأْتُوا﴾: the fāʾ is al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an implied condition), and an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿بِكِتابٍ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿مِنْ عِنْدِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of كتاب. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾: the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, with no grammatical position. ﴿هُوَ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿أَهْدى﴾: khabar (predicate); the clause is a second naʿt of كتاب. ﴿مِنْهُما﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to أهدى. ﴿أَتَّبِعْهُ﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) as the answer to the request (jawāb al-ṭalab); the hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil is latent. ﴿إِنْ﴾: a jussive conditional particle. ﴿كُنْتُمْ﴾: an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the tāʾ is its noun. ﴿صادِقِينَ﴾: its khabar; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position, and the apodosis is omitted.

daas-irab:50-50.t: ﴿فَإِنْ﴾: the fāʾ is a resumptive particle. ﴿إِنَّ﴾ «[Translator's note: so in the source; the conditional particle here is إِنْ.]»: a jussive conditional particle. ﴿لَمْ يَسْتَجِيبُوا﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لم, and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿لَكَ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿فَاعْلَمْ﴾: the fāʾ is linking (rābiṭa), and an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿أَنَّما﴾: [أنّ] restrained [from governing] by the restraining [mā] (kāffa wa-makfūfa); the clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). ﴿يَتَّبِعُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb and its fāʿil. ﴿أَهْواءَهُمْ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and the clause أنما يتبعون.. is an interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) standing in place of the two objects of اعلم. The wāw is a resumptive particle. ﴿وَمَنْ﴾: an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿أَضَلُّ﴾: its khabar (predicate); the nominal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿مِمَّنِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to أضل. ﴿اتَّبَعَ﴾: a past verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿هَواهُ﴾: mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of من. ﴿بِغَيْرِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿هُدىً﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾: the Name of Majesty is genitive by من, and both are attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of هدى. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ﴾: إنّ, and the Name of Majesty is its noun. ﴿لا﴾: negative. ﴿يَهْدِي﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿الْقَوْمَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi. ﴿الظَّالِمِينَ﴾: a naʿt of القوم; the verbal clause is the khabar of إنّ, and the nominal clause is resumptive.

daas-irab:51-51.t:
﴿وَلَقَدْ﴾: its i'rab has preceded in ayah 43. ﴿وَصَّلْنا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿لَهُمُ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿الْقَوْلَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the answer to the implied oath, with no grammatical position. ﴿لَعَلَّهُمْ﴾: لعلّ and its noun. ﴿يَتَذَكَّرُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb and its fāʿil.
The verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of لعلّ, and the nominal clause is causal (taʿlīl), with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:52-52.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾: a relative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿آتَيْناهُمُ﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its first object. ﴿الْكِتابَ﴾: second mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the verbal clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين. ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِهِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿هُمْ﴾: mubtadaʾ. ﴿بِهِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb after them. ﴿يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of هم, and the nominal clause الذين.. is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:53-53.t:
﴿وَإِذا﴾: the wāw is a resumptive particle, and إذا is temporal, conditional, non-jussive. ﴿يُتْلى﴾: a passive imperfect verb, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is in the position of genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿قالُوا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the answer of إذا, with no grammatical position. ﴿آمَنَّا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿بِهِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the verbal clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿إِنَّهُ﴾: إنّ and its noun. ﴿الْحَقُّ﴾: the khabar (predicate) of إنّ. ﴿مِنْ رَبِّنا﴾: ḥāl (circumstantial); the nominal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.
﴿إِنَّا﴾: إنّ and its noun. ﴿كُنَّا﴾: كان and its noun. ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِهِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to what follows them. ﴿مُسْلِمِينَ﴾: the khabar of كنا; the clause كنا.. is the khabar of إنا, and the clause إنا.. is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:54-54.t: ﴿أُولئِكَ﴾: a demonstrative, mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿يُؤْتَوْنَ﴾: a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). ﴿أَجْرَهُمْ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿مَرَّتَيْنِ﴾: a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (nāʾib mafʿūl muṭlaq, standing in for the absolute object). ﴿بِما﴾: the bāʾ is a preposition and ما is maṣdariyya. ﴿صَبَرُوا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from ما and the verb is in the position of genitive by the bāʾ, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb يؤتون. ﴿وَيَدْرَؤُنَ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿بِالْحَسَنَةِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿السَّيِّئَةَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi. The wāw is a conjunction. ﴿وَمِمَّا﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb ينفقون. ﴿رَزَقْناهُمْ﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil and its object; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of ما. ﴿يُنْفِقُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to the clause يؤتون, so it is in the position of nominative like it.

daas-irab:55-55.t: ﴿وَإِذا﴾: the wāw is a resumptive particle, and إذا is temporal, conditional, non-jussive. ﴿سَمِعُوا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿اللَّغْوَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the verbal clause is in the position of genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿أَعْرَضُوا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿عَنْهُ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is the answer of إذا, with no grammatical position. And the clause إذا.. is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction. ﴿وَقالُوا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿لَنا﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate). ﴿أَعْمالُنا﴾: a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the nominal clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿وَلَكُمْ أَعْمالُكُمْ﴾: conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿سَلامٌ﴾: mubtadaʾ. ﴿عَلَيْكُمْ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the khabar; the nominal clause is the object of the saying. ﴿لا﴾: negative. ﴿نَبْتَغِي﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿الْجاهِلِينَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:56-56.t:
﴿إِنَّكَ﴾: إنّ and its noun. ﴿لا﴾: negative. ﴿تَهْدِي﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿مَنْ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of إنك, and the nominal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿أَحْبَبْتَ﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَلكِنَّ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and a particle resembling the verb. ﴿اللَّهَ﴾: the Name of Majesty is its noun. ﴿يَهْدِي﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿مَنْ﴾: mafʿūl bihi; the verbal clause is the khabar of لكنّ, and the nominal clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿يَشاءُ﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent.
The clause is the ṣila. ﴿وَهُوَ أَعْلَمُ﴾: the wāw is circumstantial, and a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar. ﴿بِالْمُهْتَدِينَ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) أعلم; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:57-57.t:
﴿وَقالُوا﴾: the wāw is a resumptive particle. ﴿قالُوا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive. ﴿إِنْ﴾: a jussive conditional particle. ﴿نَتَّبِعِ﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) because it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿الْهُدى﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position.
﴿مَعَكَ﴾: an adverb of place. ﴿نُتَخَطَّفْ﴾: a passive imperfect verb, jussive because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent. ﴿مِنْ أَرْضِنا﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; and إن and what follows it are the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿أَوَلَمْ﴾: the hamza is disapproving interrogation (istifhām inkārī), and the wāw is a resumptive particle. ﴿نُمَكِّنْ﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive by لم, and the fāʿil is latent. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿حَرَماً﴾: mafʿūl bihi. ﴿آمِناً﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of حرما; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿يُجْبى﴾: a passive imperfect verb. ﴿إِلَيْهِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿ثَمَراتُ﴾: nāʾib fāʿil. ﴿كُلِّ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿شَيْءٍ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is a second naʿt of حرما. ﴿رِزْقاً﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿مِنْ لَدُنَّا﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to رزقا. ﴿وَلكِنَّ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and a particle resembling the verb. ﴿أَكْثَرَهُمْ﴾: the noun of لكنّ. ﴿لا﴾: negative. ﴿يَعْلَمُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of لكنّ, and the nominal clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it.

daas-irab:58-58.t: ﴿وَكَمْ﴾: the wāw is a resumptive particle. ﴿كَمْ﴾: predicative (khabariyya), in the position of accusative as a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿أَهْلَكْنا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿مِنْ قَرْيَةٍ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, the tamyīz (specification) of كم; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿بَطِرَتْ﴾: a past verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿مَعِيشَتَها﴾: mafʿūl bihi; the clause is a naʿt (adjective) of قرية. ﴿فَتِلْكَ مَساكِنُهُمْ﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); the nominal clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿لَمْ تُسْكَنْ﴾: a passive imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لم, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِهِمْ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿إِلَّا﴾: a particle of exception. ﴿قَلِيلًا﴾: a naʿt of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿وَ﴾: the wāw is circumstantial. ﴿كُنَّا﴾: كان and its noun. ﴿نَحْنُ﴾: a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl). ﴿الْوارِثِينَ﴾: its khabar; the clause is a ḥāl.

daas-irab:59-59.t: ﴿وَما﴾: the wāw is a resumptive particle; ما is negative. ﴿كانَ﴾: an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb. ﴿رَبُّكَ﴾: its noun. ﴿مُهْلِكَ﴾: its khabar (predicate). ﴿الْقُرى﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿حَتَّى﴾: a particle of limit (ghāya) and genitive. ﴿يَبْعَثَ﴾: an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implicit أن after حتى; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from the implicit أن and what follows it is in the position of genitive by حتى, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) مهلك. ﴿فِي أُمِّها﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿رَسُولًا﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿يَتْلُوا﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿آياتِنا﴾: mafʿūl bihi; the clause is a naʿt (adjective) of رسولا. ﴿وَما﴾: the wāw is a conjunction. ﴿ما﴾: negative. ﴿كُنَّا﴾: كان and its noun. ﴿مُهْلِكِي﴾: its khabar. ﴿الْقُرى﴾: muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿إِلَّا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿وَ﴾: the wāw is circumstantial. ﴿أَهْلُها ظالِمُونَ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:60-60.t: ﴿وَما﴾: ما is a jussive conditional noun, mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿أُوتِيتُمْ﴾: a passive past verb in the position of jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the tāʾ is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). ﴿مِنْ شَيْءٍ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿فَمَتاعُ﴾: the fāʾ is linking (rābiṭa), and the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ. ﴿الْحَياةِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿الدُّنْيا﴾: naʿt (adjective); the nominal clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and the two clauses of the protasis and the apodosis are the khabar of the mubtadaʾ ما. ﴿وَزِينَتُها﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to متاع. ﴿وَما﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and ما is a relative noun, mubtadaʾ. ﴿عِنْدَ﴾: an adverb of place. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾: the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿خَيْرٌ﴾: the khabar of the mubtadaʾ; the nominal clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَأَبْقى﴾: conjoined to خير. ﴿أَفَلا﴾: the hamza is a particle of disapproving interrogation (istifhām inkārī), and the fāʾ is a resumptive particle. ﴿لا﴾: negative. ﴿تَعْقِلُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent). The verbal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:61-61.t: ﴿أَفَمَنْ﴾: the hamza is a particle of disapproving interrogation (istifhām inkārī), and the fāʾ is a conjunction. ﴿مِنَ﴾ «[Translator's note: so vocalized in the source; the word is the relative مَنْ.]»: a relative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿وَعَدْناهُ﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its object; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of من. ﴿وَعْداً﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿حَسَناً﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of وعدا. ﴿فَهُوَ لاقِيهِ﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a mubtadaʾ and its khabar (predicate); the nominal clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿كَمَنْ﴾: من is relative, and [the preposition and its genitive noun] are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ من. ﴿مَتَّعْناهُ﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil and its object; the clause is the ṣila of من. ﴿مَتاعَ﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq. ﴿الْحَياةِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿الدُّنْيا﴾: naʿt. ﴿ثُمَّ﴾: a conjunction. ﴿هُوَ﴾: mubtadaʾ. ﴿يَوْمَ﴾: an adverb of time. ﴿الْقِيامَةِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿مِنَ الْمُحْضَرِينَ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ; the nominal clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:62-62.t: ﴿وَيَوْمَ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction. ﴿يَوْمَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being "اذكر يوم" (remember the day). ﴿يُنادِيهِمْ﴾: an imperfect verb and its object, and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is in the position of genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿فَيَقُولُ﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿أَيْنَ﴾: an interrogative noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, in the position of accusative as an adverb of place, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate). ﴿شُرَكائِيَ﴾: a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the nominal clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾: a relative noun, naʿt (adjective) of شركائي. ﴿كُنْتُمْ﴾: كان and its noun. ﴿تَزْعُمُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of كنتم, and the clause كنتم is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. The two objects of تزعمون are omitted because what precedes them indicates them.

daas-irab:63-63.t: ﴿قالَ الَّذِينَ﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿حَقَّ﴾: a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa. ﴿عَلَيْهِمُ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿الْقَوْلُ﴾: fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين. ﴿رَبَّنا﴾: the one addressed (munādā), in construct. ﴿هؤُلاءِ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾: badal (substitute). ﴿أَغْوَيْنا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿أَغْوَيْناهُمْ﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil and its object; the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ هؤلاء. ﴿كَما﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿غَوَيْنا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿ثم﴾: conjunctive. ﴿تَبَرَّأْنا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿إِلَيْكَ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿ما﴾: negative. ﴿كانُوا﴾: كان and its noun. ﴿إِيَّانا﴾: a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿يَعْبُدُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of كانوا, and the clause ما كانوا.. is a second ḥāl.

daas-irab:64-64.t:
﴿وَقِيلَ﴾: the wāw is a resumptive particle. ﴿قِيلَ﴾: a passive past verb. ﴿ادْعُوا﴾: an imperative verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿شُرَكاءَكُمْ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿فَدَعَوْهُمْ﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb, its fāʿil and its object. ﴿فَلَمْ﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction. ﴿يَسْتَجِيبُوا﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لم, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it.
﴿وَرَأَوُا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; رأوا is a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿الْعَذابَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi; the clause is conjoined. ﴿لَوْ﴾: a non-jussive conditional particle. ﴿أَنَّهُمْ﴾: أنّ and its noun. ﴿كانُوا﴾: كان and its noun. ﴿يَهْتَدُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of كانوا, and the clause كانوا.. is the khabar of أنّ. The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from أنّ, its noun and its khabar is in the position of nominative as the fāʿil of an omitted verb.

daas-irab:65-65.t: ﴿وَيَوْمَ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; يوم is mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, اذكر (remember). ﴿يُنادِيهِمْ﴾: an imperfect verb and its object, and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is in the position of genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿فَيَقُولُ﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿ماذا﴾: an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿أَجَبْتُمُ﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿الْمُرْسَلِينَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).

daas-irab:66-66.t: ﴿فَعَمِيَتْ﴾: the fāʾ is a resumptive particle; عميت is a passive past verb «[Translator's note: so in the source; عَمِيَتْ is in the active voice, and الأنباء is its fāʿil (agent).]», and the tāʾ is for the feminine. ﴿عَلَيْهِمُ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿الْأَنْباءُ﴾: nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾: an adverb of time annexed to its like. ﴿فَهُمْ﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿لا﴾: negative. ﴿يَتَساءَلُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it.

daas-irab:67-67.t: ﴿فَأَمَّا﴾: the fāʾ is a resumptive particle. ﴿أما﴾: a particle of condition and detailing (tafṣīl). ﴿مَنْ﴾: a relative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿تابَ﴾: a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of من. ﴿وَآمَنَ﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to تاب. ﴿وَعَمِلَ﴾: also conjoined. ﴿صالِحاً﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿فَعَسى﴾: the fāʾ falls in the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). ﴿عسى﴾: an inflexible (jāmid) past verb whose noun is latent. ﴿أَنْ﴾: a particle that puts in the accusative. ﴿يَكُونَ﴾: an incomplete (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by أن, and its noun is latent. ﴿مِنَ الْمُفْلِحِينَ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar (predicate) of يكون; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from أن and what follows it is the khabar of عسى, the clause عسى.. is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ من, and the clause أما من.. is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:68-68.t: ﴿وَرَبُّكَ﴾: the wāw is a resumptive particle, and a mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿يَخْلُقُ﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ. ﴿ما﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿يَشاءُ﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of ما. ﴿وَيَخْتارُ﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to يخلق. ﴿ما﴾: negative. ﴿كانَ﴾: an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb. ﴿لَهُمُ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) its omitted, fronted khabar. ﴿الْخِيَرَةُ﴾: its postponed noun; the verbal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿سُبْحانَ﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾: the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَتَعالى﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and a past verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿عَمَّا﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿يُشْرِكُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila of ما.

daas-irab:69-69.t: ﴿وَرَبُّكَ﴾: the wāw is a resumptive particle, and a mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿يَعْلَمُ﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿ما﴾: a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿تُكِنُّ صُدُورُهُمْ﴾: an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of ما. ﴿وَما﴾: the wāw is a conjunction. ﴿ما﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿يُعْلِنُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila of ما.

daas-irab:70-70.t: ﴿وَهُوَ اللَّهُ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿لا﴾: the lā of generic negation, operating like إنّ. ﴿إِلهَ﴾: its noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, in the position of accusative. ﴿إِلَّا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿هُوَ﴾: badal (substitute) from the pronoun latent in the omitted khabar of لا; the nominal clause is a second khabar of the mubtadaʾ هو. ﴿لَهُ﴾: a fronted khabar. ﴿الْحَمْدُ﴾: a postponed mubtadaʾ; the nominal clause is a third khabar of the mubtadaʾ هو. ﴿فِي الْأُولى﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) الحمد. ﴿وَالْآخِرَةِ﴾: conjoined to الأولى. ﴿وَلَهُ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and a fronted khabar. ﴿الْحُكْمُ﴾: a postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَإِلَيْهِ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and [the preposition and its genitive noun] are attached to what follows them. ﴿تُرْجَعُونَ﴾: a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:71-71.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾: an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿أَرَأَيْتُمْ﴾: the hamza is a particle of interrogation, and a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿إِنْ﴾: a jussive conditional particle. ﴿جَعَلَ﴾: a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, in the position of jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). ﴿اللَّهُ﴾: the Name of Majesty, fāʿil; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿عَلَيْكُمُ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿اللَّيْلَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿سَرْمَداً﴾: second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿إِلى يَوْمِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to جعل. ﴿الْقِيامَةِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿مَنْ إِلهٌ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate). ﴿غَيْرُ﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of إله. ﴿اللَّهُ﴾: the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿يَأْتِيكُمْ﴾: an imperfect verb and its object, and the fāʿil is latent. ﴿بِضِياءٍ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the verbal clause is a naʿt of إله. ﴿أَفَلا﴾: the hamza is a particle of disapproving interrogation (istifhām inkārī), the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, and لا is negative. ﴿تَسْمَعُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

farraa:6-6.t: His saying: ﴿وَيَري فِرْعَوْنُ وَهَامَانَ وَجُنُودُهُمَا﴾: this is how the companions of ʿAbd Allāh read it, with the yāʾ and the nominative. The people after them read it with the nūn: ﴿وَنُرِيَ فِرْعَوْنَ وَهَامَانَ وَجُنُودَهُمَا﴾ in the accusative. Had it been read with the yāʾ and Pharaoh in the accusative, meaning ﴿ويُرِىَ اللهُ فرعون﴾ ("and that Allah should show Pharaoh"), the verb would belong to Allah; but I have not heard anyone read it so.

farraa:8-8.t: His saying: ﴿عَدُوّاً وَحَزَناً﴾: this is [the reading] of the companions of ʿAbd Allāh [Translator's note: presumably ḥuznan, as the contrast that follows implies], and the generality [read] ﴿حَزَنا﴾. It seems that al-ḥuzn is the noun — like grief and the like — and that al-ḥazan is the maṣdar (verbal noun). The two are like al-ʿudm and al-ʿadam.

farraa:9-9.t:
His saying: ﴿وَقَالَتِ ٱمْرَأَةُ فِرْعَوْنَ قُرَّةُ عَيْنٍ لِّي وَلَكَ﴾: You put ﴿قُرّةُ عَيْنٍ﴾ in the nominative by implying (هو) (he is); the like of it in the Quran is frequent, put in the nominative by an implied pronoun.
His saying: ﴿لاَ تَقْتُلُوهُ﴾: in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: (لا تقتلوه قُرَّةُ عين لى ولك) ("Do not kill him — a comfort of the eye for me and for you"). I have mentioned this only because I heard the one called Ibn Marwān al-Suddī mention from al-Kalbī from Abū Ṣāliḥ from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: she said (قُرَّةَ عَيْنٍ لِّي وَلَكَ لاَ) ("a comfort of the eye for me — and for you, no"), and that is a solecism (laḥn). The reading of ʿAbd Allāh strengthens you in rejecting it.
His saying: ﴿وَهُمْ لاَ يَشْعُرُونَ﴾ means the Children of Israel; that is one view. It may also be that this is the saying of Allah: and they did not perceive that Mūsā was the one who would strip them of their kingdom.

farraa:10-10.t: His saying: ﴿وَأَصْبَحَ فُؤَادُ أُمِّ مُوسَىٰ فَارِغاً﴾: it became empty for her worry, so nothing mixed with the worry over Mūsā. His saying ﴿إِن كَادَتْ لَتُبْدِي بِهِ﴾ means: [disclose] the name of Mūsā, that he was her son. That is because her breast became constricted at the saying of Pharaoh's people, "He is Pharaoh's son", so she almost disclosed [it], i.e. revealed it. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: ﴿إن كادت لَتُشعِرُ بِهِ﴾ ("she almost made it known"). Abū al-ʿAbbās related to us: Muḥammad related to us: al-Farrāʾ related to us, saying: Ibn Abī Yaḥyā related to me, with a chain of his, that Faḍāla ibn ʿUbayd al-Anṣārī, one of the Companions of the Prophet, upon him be peace, read (وَأَصْبَحَ فُؤَادُ أُمِّ مُوسَىٰ فَزِعاً) ("terrified"), from al-fazaʿ (terror).

farraa:11-11.t: His saying: ﴿وَقَالَتْ لأُخْتِهِ قُصِّيهِ﴾: follow his trail. ﴿فَبَصُرَتْ بِهِ عَن جُنُبٍ﴾: he says: she was on the bank of the river until she saw that Pharaoh's people had picked him up. His saying ﴿وَهُمْ لاَ يَشْعُرُونَ﴾ means: Pharaoh's people did not perceive his sister.

farraa:12-12.t: His saying: ﴿وَحَرَّمْنَا عَلَيْهِ ٱلْمَرَاضِعَ﴾: he says: We prevented him from accepting any breast except his mother's breast.

farraa:15-15.t:
His saying: ﴿وَدَخَلَ ٱلْمَدِينَةَ عَلَىٰ حِينِ غَفْلَةٍ﴾: He said (عَلَى) and did not say "he entered the city at a time of heedlessness", although you say "I entered the city when its people were heedless" and do not say "I entered it ʿalā when its people were heedless". That is because "heedlessness" sufficed in place of "time"; do you not see that you say "I entered upon heedlessness (ʿalā ghafla)" and "I came upon heedlessness"? So since (حين) was like a surplus in the speech, and the meaning is "in heedlessness", (على) was brought in for it; and had it not been there, it would be correct. Similar is the saying of Allah ﴿عَلَى فَتْرَةٍ مِنَ الرُسُلِ﴾; had it been "ʿalā ḥīni fatratin min al-rusul" it would be like this. Similar is the saying of al-ʿUjayz:
..... ومن يكن * فتى عامَ عام الماءِ فهْو كبير
(… and whoever was a youth in the year — the year of the water — is old [now].)
Thus al-ʿUqaylī recited it to me; the first "year" is surplus.
His saying: ﴿فَوَكَزَهُ مُوسَىٰ﴾ means: he punched him (lakazahu). In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: ﴿فَنكَزهُ﴾; and wahazahu is also a dialectal form; all are the same. His saying ﴿فَقَضَىٰ عَلَيْهِ﴾ means: he killed him.
Mūsā regretted it, sought Allah's forgiveness, and He forgave him.

farraa:17-17.t: His saying: ﴿قَالَ رَبِّ بِمَآ أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيَّ فَلَنْ أَكُونَ ظَهِيراً لِّلْمُجْرِمِينَ﴾: Ibn ʿAbbās said: he did not make an exception [i.e. say "if Allah wills"], so he was put to trial. He made (لَنْ) a statement by Mūsā. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: (فَلاَ تَجْعَلْنِى ظَهِيراً) ("so do not make me a supporter"). Accordingly ﴿لَنْ أَكُونَ﴾ may in this sense be a supplication from Mūsā: "O Allah, I shall never be a supporter for them", so it is a supplication. That is because the man of his own party was met by a man after he had killed the first one, and he subjected the one of Mūsā's party to forced labour. Mūsā passed by him in that state and he cried out to him — i.e. called for his help — and Mūsā said to him: ﴿إِنَّكَ لَغَوِيٌّ مُّبِينٌ﴾, i.e. I killed a man yesterday and you call me to another! He came towards the two of them, and the man of his party thought he meant [to strike] him, so he said ﴿أَتُرِيدُ أَن تَقْتُلَنِي كَمَا قَتَلْتَ نَفْساً بِٱلأَمْسِ﴾. Pharaoh had not known who killed the first Copt. So the second Copt let Mūsā's companion go from his hand and reported that Mūsā was the killer. That is the saying of Ibn ʿAbbās: he was put to trial in that it was his own companion who pointed him out.

farraa:22-22.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلَمَّا تَوَجَّهَ تِلْقَآءَ مَدْيَنَ﴾: he means: he headed for the water of Madyan. Madyan is not declined (lam tuṣraf) because it is the name of that town. The poet said:
رُهبانُ مَدْيَن لو رأوكِ تَنَزَّلُوا * والعُصْمُ من شَعَفِ العقول الفادر
(The monks of Madyan, had they seen you, would come down, and so would the white-legged ibexes from the crags of the high peaks.)
His saying: ﴿أَن يَهْدِيَنِي سَوَآءَ ٱلسَّبِيلِ﴾: the road to Madyan; he did not know its way.

farraa:23-23.t: His saying, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿وَوَجَدَ مِن دُونِهِمُ ٱمْرَأَتَينِ تَذُودَانِ﴾: they were holding back their sheep. It is not permissible to say "dhudtu al-rajul" meaning "I held the man back". Al-dhiyād is holding back of sheep only because when any of the sheep or camels wants to stray and go off and you turn it back, that is dhawd, which is holding back. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: (وَدُونَهُمُ امْرَأَتَانِ حَابِسَتَانِ) ("and beyond them two women holding back [their flocks]"). He asked them about their holding back, and they said: we are not strong enough to water along with the people until they drive off [their flocks]. So he went to the people of the water and asked them to give him a bucket. They said: draw water, if you are strong enough — and the bucket was carried by forty men or thereabouts. He drew water by himself alone and watered their sheep. That is the saying of one of the two girls: ﴿إنَّ خَيْرَ مَنِ اسْتَأْجَرْتَ القَوِىُّ الأَمِينُ﴾. His strength was his drawing out the bucket alone; and his trustworthiness was that one of the two girls said, "My father calls you", and he rose with her; she walked in front of him, and the wind blew her clothes and pressed them against her body, so he said to her: "Walk behind; and if I go astray, guide me." So she walked behind him; that was his trustworthiness.

farraa:27-27.t: His saying: ﴿عَلَىٰ أَن تَأْجُرَنِي ثَمَانِيَ حِجَجٍ﴾: he says: that you make my reward [for my daughter] that you tend my sheep for me for eight years. ﴿فَإِنْ أَتْمَمْتَ عَشْراً فَمِنْ عِندِكَ﴾: he says: that is voluntary. Ibn ʿAbbās mentioned that he completed the longer and better of the two terms.

farraa:28-28.t:
His saying: ﴿أَيَّمَا ٱلأَجَلَيْنِ قَضَيْتُ﴾: He placed (ما), which is one of the connectives (ṣilāt) of the conditional, with (أى). In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: (أىَّ الأجلين مَا قَضَيْتُ فَلاَ عُدْوَانَ عَلَىَّ), and this is more frequent in the speech of the Arabs than the first.
The poet said:
وأيَّهما ما أتْبَعَنَّ فإننى * حَريصٌ على إثْرِ الذى أنَا تابعُ
(Whichever of the two I follow, I am eager on the track of the one I follow.)
Al-Kisāʾī heard a Bedouin say: "Whichever of them takes it rides on whichever of them" — meaning in a game of theirs. That is also permissible and good.

farraa:29-29.t: His saying: ﴿أَوْ جَذْوَةٍ مِّنَ ٱلنَّارِ﴾: ʿĀṣim read it (أَوْ جَذْوَةٍ) with fatḥa, and the reading [of others] is with kasra on the jīm, or [140/a] with ḍamma on it. It is like awṭaʾtuka ʿishwatan, ʿushwatan and ʿashwatan (I led you blindly), and al-raghwa, al-rughwa and al-righwa (froth). Of the same kind is rabwa, rubwa and ribwa (hillock).

farraa:32-32.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱضْمُمْ إِلَيْكَ جَنَاحَكَ مِنَ ٱلرُّهْبِ﴾ and ﴿الرَّهَبِ﴾: the people of Medina read it ﴿الرّهَب﴾, and ʿĀṣim and al-Aʿmash (الرُّهْبِ).
His saying: ﴿فَذَانِكَ بُرْهَانَانِ﴾: the readers agree on the light nūn in ﴿ذَانِكَ﴾, but many of the Arabs say ﴿فذانّك﴾, ﴿وهذانّ﴾ qāʾimān, and ﴿واللذانِّ يأْتِيانهِا مِنْكُمْ﴾, doubling the nūn.
His saying: ﴿وَٱضْمُمْ إِلَيْكَ جَنَاحَكَ﴾: he means his staff in this place. Al-janāḥ in the other place is what lies between the lower end of the upper arm and the rufgh, which is the armpit.

farraa:34-34.t: His saying: ﴿رِدْءاً يُصَدِّقُنِي﴾ is read in the jussive and in the nominative. Whoever puts it in the nominative makes it a ṣila (qualifying clause) of al-ridʾ; whoever puts it in the jussive does so on [the basis of] the condition. Al-ridʾ is help; you say: ardaʾtu al-rajul, I helped him. The people of Medina say (رِداً يُصّدِّقْنِى) without hamza, with the jussive on [the basis of] the condition: "send him with me, [and] he will confirm me", like ﴿يَرِثُنِى وَيَرِث﴾.

farraa:38-38.t:
His saying: ﴿فَأَوْقِدْ لِي يٰهَامَانُ عَلَى ٱلطِّينِ﴾: he says: bake bricks for me — it is al-ujūr and al-ājurr. And he recited:
كأنَّ عينيه من الغُؤور * قَلْتان فى جَوف صَفاً منقور * عُولى بالطين وبالأجور *
(As if his two eyes, from their sunkenness, were two rock-pools in the hollow of a carved rock, raised up with clay and baked bricks.)

farraa:48-48.t:
His saying: ﴿قَالُواْ سِحْرَانِ تَظَاهَرَا﴾: they mean the Torah and the Quran. And it is said ﴿سَاحِران تَظَاهَرَا﴾ ("two sorcerers supporting each other"): they mean Muhammad and Mūsā, may Allah bless them both and grant them peace. ʿĀṣim and al-Aʿmash read (سِحْرانِ).
Abū al-ʿAbbās related to us, saying: Muḥammad related to us, saying: al-Farrāʾ related to us, saying: more than one person related to me from Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Khālid from Abū Razīn that he read (سِحْرانِ تَظَاهَرا).
He said: Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna said from Ḥumayd: Mujāhid said: I asked Ibn ʿAbbās, while ʿIkrima was with him, and he did not answer me. When it was the third time, ʿIkrima said: you have pressed him too much [about] (سَاحِرَان تَظَاهَرَا), and Ibn ʿAbbās did not object — or he said: had he objected to it he would have changed it. ʿIkrima used to read (سِحْرَانِ) without an alif, and he would adduce as proof His saying: ﴿قُلْ فأْتُوا بكِتابٍ مِنْ عندِ الله هُوَ أَهْدَى منهما أَتَّبِعْهُ﴾. The people of Medina and al-Ḥasan read it (سَاحِرَان تظَاهَرَا).

farraa:49-49.t: His saying: ﴿أَتَّبِعْهُ﴾ is nominative [i.e. if read attabiʿuhu], being a ṣila of "a book" because it is indefinite; and if you put it in the jussive — which is the [preferred] way — you make it the apodosis of the command.

farraa:51-51.t: His saying: ﴿وَلَقَدْ وَصَّلْنَا لَهُمُ ٱلْقَوْلَ﴾: he says: We sent down to them the Quran, one part of it following another.

farraa:53-53.t:
His saying: ﴿إنَّا كُنَّا مِن قَبْلِهِ مُسْلِمِينَ﴾: It may be asked: how did they submit (aslamū) before the Quran and before Muhammad ﷺ? That is because they used to find the description of the Prophet ﷺ in their scripture, and they believed in it; that was their submission.
And in ﴿مِن قَبْلِهِ﴾ this hāʾ is for the Prophet, upon him be peace. Had the hāʾ been an allusion to the Quran, it would be correct, because they had said: "It is the truth from our Lord"; so the hāʾ here can be for the Quran as well as for Muhammad ﷺ.

farraa:56-56.t:
His saying: ﴿إِنَّكَ لاَ تَهْدِي مَنْ أَحْبَبْتَ﴾: love here may be taken in two ways. One of them: you do not guide whom you love because of kinship.
The other way: he means: you do not guide whomever you would love to be guided — like your saying "you do not guide whom you wish" — as you see frequently in the Revelation: ﴿وَلَـٰكِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَهْدِي مَن يَشَآءُ﴾ to guide.

farraa:57-57.t:
His saying: ﴿أَوَلَمْ نُمَكِّن لَّهُمْ حَرَماً آمِناً﴾: Quraysh said: O Muhammad, nothing prevents us [Translator's note: the source has «يا يمنعنا», evidently for «ما يمنعنا»] from believing in you and confirming you except that the Arabs are on our religion, so we fear that we will be wiped out if we believe in you. So Allah sent down ﴿أَوَلَمْ نُمَكِّن لَّهُمْ﴾ — [i.e. have We not] settled them in ﴿حَرَماً آمِناً﴾, where whoever enters it does not fear that a ḥadd punishment or retaliation will be applied to him? So how do they fear that the Arabs will deem it lawful to fight them in it?
His saying: ﴿يُجْبَىٰ إِلَيْهِ ثَمَرَاتُ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ﴾ and ﴿تُجْبَى﴾: yujbā is masculine even though "fruits" is feminine, because you have separated the two with ilayhi, as the poet said: [140/b]
إنّ امرءًا غَرَّه منكُنَّ واحدُةٌ * بعدى وَبعدك فى الدنيا لمغرور
(A man whom one of you [women] has deluded, after me and after you, in this world, is surely deluded.)
And another said:
لقد ولدَ الأُخيطلَ أُمُّ سَوْء * على قِمَع اسْتِها صُلُب وشَامُ
(An evil mother bore little al-Akhṭal, with crosses and tattoo-marks on her rump.)

farraa:58-58.t:
His saying: ﴿وَكَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا مِن قَرْيَةٍ بَطِرَتْ مَعِيشَتَهَا﴾: baṭirathā means: it was ungrateful for it and lost it. Your putting "livelihood" in the accusative is of the same kind as His saying ﴿إلاّ مَنْ سَفِهَ نَفْسَهُ﴾. The meaning, and Allah knows best, is only: its livelihood made it insolent (abṭarathā maʿīshatuhā), as you say: "your wealth made you insolent, and you were insolent over it (baṭirtahu)", and "your opinion made you foolish, and you were foolish in it (safihtahu)". "Livelihood" is mentioned because the verb originally belonged to it, and was then transferred to that to which it is annexed. Its accusative is like the accusative in His saying ﴿فإنْ طِبْنَ لَكُمْ عَنْ شَىءٍ مِنْهُ نَفْساً﴾: do you not see that "being pleased" belonged to the soul, and when you transferred it to the owner of the soul, "soul" came out in the accusative to specify the meaning of "being pleased"? Likewise ﴿ضقنا به ذَْرْعاً﴾: the meaning was only "our capacity (dharʿunā) was straitened by it".
His saying: ﴿لَمْ تُسْكَن مِّن بَعْدِهِمْ إِلاَّ قَلِيلاً﴾: its meaning is: they fell into ruin after them, and none of them was inhabited except a little, the rest being in ruin. You see the wording as though they were inhabited a little and then abandoned, but the meaning is as I have told you. Similar is: "I did not give you your dirhams except a little", meaning only: except a little of them.

farraa:59-59.t: His saying: ﴿حَتَّىٰ يَبْعَثَ فِيۤ أُمِّهَا﴾: the Mother of Towns (umm al-qurā) is Mecca. It is called the Mother of Towns only because the earth — according to what they mention — was spread out from beneath it.

farraa:66-66.t: His saying: ﴿فَهُمْ لاَ يَتَسَآءَلُونَ﴾: Someone may say: Allah said ﴿وَأَقْبَلَ بَعْضُهُمْ عَلَى بَعْضٍ يَتَسَاءَلُونَ﴾, so how did He say here ﴿فَهُمْ لاَ يَتَسَآءَلُونَ﴾? The exegesis says: the arguments were obscured for them on that day, so they fell silent; that is His saying ﴿فَهُمْ لاَ يَتَسَآءَلُونَ﴾ at that hour, and they do not speak.

farraa:67-67.t: His saying: ﴿فَعَسَىٰ أَن يَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلْمُفْلِحِينَ﴾: As for every instance of ﴿عَسَى﴾ in the Quran, it has been mentioned to us that it is binding (wājiba, i.e. certain to happen).

farraa:68-68.t: His saying: ﴿مَا كَانَ لَهُمُ ٱلْخِيَرَةُ﴾: one says al-khiyara and al-khīra [Translator's note: the two forms are not distinguished in the vowelling of the source], and al-ṭiyara and al-ṭīra. The Arabs say: "Give me the choice (al-khayra) of them" and "al-khiyara". All of that is the thing chosen, whether man, woman or beast; any of these three [forms] is sound in it.

farraa:71-71.t: His saying: ﴿إِن جَعَلَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيْكُمُ ٱلْلَّيْلَ سَرْمَداً﴾: perpetual, with no day along with it. They say: "I left him sarmadan samdan" — an itbāʿ (rhyming echo-word).

farraa:73-73.t: His saying: ﴿جَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلْلَّيْلَ وَٱلنَّهَارَ لِتَسْكُنُواْ فِيهِ وَلِتَبتَغُواْ مِن فَضْلِهِ﴾: If you wish, you may make the hāʾ refer to the night specifically and imply for the seeking another hāʾ for the day; that is permissible. And if you wish, you may make the night and the day like two actions, since they are darkness and light, so the hāʾ in (فيه) refers to both of them together, as you say: "your coming and your going annoy me (yuʾdhīnī)", because they are an action, and an action's plural and dual are referred back to the singular; so that is correct.

farraa:76-76.t:
His saying: ﴿إِنَّ قَارُونَ كَانَ مِن قَوْمِ مُوسَىٰ فَبَغَىٰ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾: he was his cousin (the son of his paternal uncle). ﴿فَبَغَىٰ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾: his transgression against them was that he said: if prophethood belongs to Mūsā, and the altar and the offering that is offered are in the hand of Hārūn, then what is there for me?
His saying: ﴿وَآتَيْنَاهُ مِنَ ٱلْكُنُوزِ مَآ إِنَّ مَفَاتِحَهُ لَتَنُوءُ بِٱلْعُصْبَةِ﴾: their weighing down (nawʾ) the band is that they burden them. The band (al-ʿuṣba) here is forty men, and mafātiḥuhu are his storehouses. The meaning is: whose keys would make the band bend (la-tunīʾu), i.e. make them lean from their weight. When you bring in the bāʾ you say: tanūʾu bihim and tunīʾu bihim, as He said ﴿آتُونى أُفرِغْ عَلَيْهِ قِطْراً﴾, the meaning being: bring me molten copper (iʾtūnī bi-qiṭrin) that I may pour on it; when you drop the bāʾ you add an alif to the beginning of the verb. Similar is ﴿فَأَجَاءَهَا المَخَاضُ﴾, whose meaning is: the labour pains brought her (jāʾa bihā). One of the people of Arabic [learning] said: the meaning is "the band would be weighed down by its keys", and the verb was transferred to the keys, as the poet said:
إن سراجاً لكريم مفخره * تَحْلَى به العَيْنُ إذا ما تَجْهَرُه
(Sirāj is noble in his glory; the eye delights in him whenever it beholds him.)
— whereas it is he who is pleasing to the eye. If he heard a transmitted report for this, then it is a valid view; otherwise the man did not know the meaning. One of the Arabs recited to me:
حتى إذا ما التأمَتْ مَوَاصِلُهْ * وناء فى شقٍّ الثِّمالِ كاهِلُهْ
(Until, when his joints had knit together and his shoulders leaned over to the left side…)
He means the archer: when he took the bow and drew, he leaned over to his side; that is his leaning (nawʾ) upon it. And we hold that the Arabs' saying "mā sāʾaka wa-nāʾaka" is from that; its meaning is "mā sāʾaka wa-anāʾaka" (what grieved you and weighed you down), except that he dropped the alif because it follows sāʾaka, just as the Arabs say: "I ate food and it was wholesome and agreeable to me (hanaʾanī wa-maraʾanī)", whose meaning, when used alone, is amraʾanī; the alif was dropped from it when it was made to follow a word without an alif.
His saying: ﴿إِذْ قَالَ لَهُ قَوْمُهُ لاَ تَفْرَحْ﴾: they mentioned that it was Mūsā who said that to him, because he [Qārūn] was of his people even though he was not of his religion. He used the plural here while it was one person, like the saying of Allah ﴿الَّذِينَ قَالَ لَهُمُ الناسُ إنَّ الناسَ قَدْ جَمَعُوا لَكُمْ﴾, whereas it was only one man from Ashjaʿ. His saying ﴿الفَرِحين﴾: had it been said al-fāriḥīn, it would be correct. It is as if al-fāriḥūn are those who will rejoice in what lies ahead of them, and al-fariḥūn are those who are in it now, like al-ṭāmiʿ and al-ṭamiʿ, al-māʾit and al-mayyit, al-sālis and al-salis. One of Banū Dubayr — who are the eloquent ones of Banū Asad — recited to me:
ممكورةٌ غَرْثى الوشاحِ السَّالِسِ * تضحك عن ذى أُشُر عُضارس
(Full-limbed, her loose sash hungry [on a slender waist], she smiles revealing serrated, cool teeth.)
Al-ʿuḍāris is the cool; it is taken from al-ʿaḍras, which is cold [hail]. One says: sālis and salis.

farraa:78-78.t:
His saying: ﴿إِنَّمَآ أُوتِيتُهُ عَلَىٰ عِلْمٍ عِندِيۤ﴾: on account of a merit I have, i.e. I was worthy of it and deserving of it, since I was given it for the excellence of my knowledge. It is also said: ﴿أُوتِيتُهُ عَلَىٰ عِلْمٍ﴾, then he said ﴿عِندِيۤ﴾, i.e. so I consider it, as He said ﴿إنَّمَا أُوتِيتُهُ عَلَى عِلْمٍ بَلْ هِى فِتْنةٌ﴾.
His saying: ﴿وَلاَ يُسْأَلُ عَن ذُنُوبِهِمُ ٱلْمُجْرِمُونَ﴾: he says: the criminal will not be asked about his sin. The hāʾ and mīm are for the criminals. He says: they will be known by their marks. It is like His saying ﴿فَيَوْمَئِذٍ لاَ يُسْأَلُ عَنْ ذَنْبِهِ إِنْسٌ وَلاَ جانٌّ﴾, then He made it clear, saying: ﴿يُعْرَفُ المُجْرِمُونَ بِسيمَاهُمْ﴾.

farraa:80-80.t: His saying: ﴿وَلاَ يُلَقَّاهَآ إِلاَّ ٱلصَّابِرُونَ﴾: he says: and none is granted [the ability] to say "the reward of Allah is better for whoever believes and does righteous deeds" except the patient. Had it been "wa-lā yulaqqāhu" it would be correct, because it is speech, and speech may be treated as feminine or masculine. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: (بَلْ هِى آيات بيِّنات), and in our reading ﴿بَلْ هُوَ آياتٌ﴾: whoever says (هى) has in mind the verses, and whoever says (هو) has in mind the Quran. Likewise ﴿تِلْكَ مِنْ أَنْبَاءِ الغَيْبِ﴾ and ﴿ذَلِكَ مِنْ أَنْبَاءِ الغَيْبِ﴾. Similar in ordinary speech: "That (dhāka) of yours has grieved me" and "That (tilka) of yours has grieved me."

farraa:82-82.t:
His saying: ﴿وَيْكَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ﴾: in the speech of the Arabs it is an affirmation (taqrīr), like a man's saying: "Do you not see the work of Allah?"
And he recited to me:
وَيْكأنْ مَنْ يكن له نَشَبٌ يُحـ * ـبَبْ وَمَنْ يَفْتقِر يعش عيشَ ضُرّ
(Do you not see: whoever has wealth is loved, and whoever becomes poor lives a life of hardship.)
Al-Farrāʾ said: a shaykh of the people of Basra told me, saying: I heard a Bedouin woman say to her husband: "Where is your son, woe to you?" He said: "Wayka-annahu behind the house", meaning: do you not see him behind the house? Some grammarians take the view that they are two words, meaning wayka annahu: he meant waylaka (woe to you), dropped the lām, and made (أنّ) take fatḥa by an implied verb, as though he said: "Woe to you, know that he is behind the house", implying (اعْلم) (know). But we have not found the Arabs making [verbs of] supposing and knowing govern anna while implied. That is because it is cancelled when it is between the two words or at the end of [141/b] the sentence, so when it is implied it is treated as left out. Do you not see that it is not permissible at the beginning [of speech] to say "O you, that you are standing (annaka qāʾim)", nor "O you, that you stood (an qumta)", meaning "I knew", "I know", "I thought" or "I think"? As for dropping the lām of (ويْلك) so that it becomes (ويك), the Arabs do say it because of its frequency in speech. ʿAntara said:
ولقد شفى نفسى وَأبرأ سُقمها * قولُ الفوارس وَيْكَ عَنْتَرَ أقدِم
(What healed my soul and cured its sickness was the horsemen's cry: "Woe to you, ʿAntar, charge!")
Others have said that the meaning of (وَىْ كأنَّ) is that (وَىْ) is separate from (كأنّ), as when you say to a man: "Way! Do you not see what is in front of you?" — he said "way", then began afresh with (كأنّ), meaning ﴿ْكَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَبْسُطُ ٱلرِّزْقَ﴾; [way] is [an expression of] wonder, and (كأنَّ) is in the sense of supposing and knowing. This is a sound view. But the Arabs did not write it separately; had it been like this, they would have written it separately. It may be that speech with it became frequent, so it was joined to what is not part of it, just as the Arabs agreed on writing ﴿يا بْنَ أُمَّ﴾ as ﴿يابْنَؤُمَّ﴾. He said: and thus I saw it in the muṣḥaf of ʿAbd Allāh, and it is so in our copies too.
His saying: ﴿لَخَسَفَ بِنَا﴾: the reading of the generality is (لَخُسِفَ). Shayba and al-Ḥasan — as far as I know — read it (لخَسَفَ بنا). In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is (لانْخُسِف بِنَا), and this is evidence for whoever reads ﴿لخُسِفَ﴾.

farraa:85-85.t: His saying: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلَّذِي فَرَضَ عَلَيْكَ﴾: he says: [the One who] sent down the Quran to you ﴿لَرَادُّكَ إلَى مَعَاد﴾. They mention that Jibrīl said: O Muhammad, do you long for your birthplace and your homeland? He said: yes. He said: so he said to him what was sent down to him: ﴿نَّ ٱلَّذِي فَرَضَ عَلَيْكَ ٱلْقُرْآنَ لَرَآدُّكَ إِلَىٰ مَعَادٍ﴾, meaning to Mecca. By al-maʿād here He meant only where you were born; it is not from al-ʿawd (returning). It may also be that His saying ﴿لرادُّكَ﴾ refers to your coming to return to Mecca, conquered for you; then al-maʿād is [an expression of] wonder: ﴿إلى مَعَادٍ﴾ — what a return! — because of what He promised him of the conquest of Mecca.

farraa:86-86.t: His saying: ﴿وَمَا كُنتَ تَرْجُوۤ أَن يُلْقَىٰ إِلَيْكَ ٱلْكِتَابُ إِلاَّ رَحْمَةً مِّن رَّبِّكَ﴾: except that your Lord had mercy on you ﴿فأنزل عليك﴾; so it is a discontinuous exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ). Its meaning is: you did not hope to know the books of the ancients and their stories, reciting them to the people of Mecca, when you were not present at them and did not witness them. The evidence for that is His saying in this sūra ﴿وَمَا كُنْتَ ثَاوِياً فى أَهْلِ مَدْيَنَ تَتْلُو عليهِم آياتِنَا﴾, i.e. you recite to the people of Mecca the stories of Madyan and Mūsā, while you were not dwelling there, staying, so that you might see it and hear it. Likewise His saying ﴿وَمَا كُنْتَ بِجَانِبِ الغَرْبِىِّ﴾, and here you are reciting their stories and their affair. This is the mercy from his Lord.

farraa:88-88.t:
His saying: ﴿كُلُّ شَيْءٍ هَالِكٌ إِلاَّ وَجْهَهُ﴾: except Him.
The poet said:
أستغفرُ الله ذنباً لَسْتُ مُحْصِيهُ * رَبّ العِبَاد إليه الوَجْهُ وَالْعَمَلُ
(I ask forgiveness of Allah for sins I cannot count — the Lord of the servants, to Whom are the face and the deed.)
I.e. to Him I direct my deeds.

muyesser-irab:8-8.t:
﴿فالتقطه آل فرعون ليكون لهم عدوا وحزنا﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ implying an omitted clause); (التقطه): a past verb, and a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (آل): a postponed fāʿil (agent); (فرعون): muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (ليكون): the lām is of consequence (al-ʿāqiba), and it has been said: of causation (taʿlīl); (يكون): an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied (muḍmara) أن after the lām, and the interpreted maṣdar (maṣdar muʾawwal) from أن and the verb is genitive (majrūr) by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿التقطه﴾; the noun (ism) of يكون is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "هو"; (لهم): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿يكون﴾; (عدوًّا): the khabar (predicate) of يكون; (حزنًا): conjoined to ﴿عدوًّا﴾.
﴿إن فرعون وهامان وجنودهما كانوا خاطئين﴾: (إن) is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and (فرعون) is its noun; ﴿وهامان وجنودهما﴾: conjoined to فرعون; the clause (كانوا) is the khabar of إن; (كان) is an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb, the wāw of the plural is its noun, and (خاطئين) is its khabar.

muyesser-irab:9-9.t:
﴿وقالت امرأت فرعون قرت عين لي ولك﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; (قالت): conjoined to ﴿فالتقطه آل فرعون﴾; ﴿امرأة فرعون﴾: fāʿil (agent) and muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (قرة عين): the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "هو قرة عين"; (لي): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted element, two naʿts (adjectives) of قرة [Translator's note: so in the source: "صفتان" (two adjectives) after only لي has been mentioned; presumably لي and لك together]; (لك): conjoined to ﴿لي﴾.
﴿لا تقتلوه عسى أن ينفعنا أو نتخذه ولدا وهم لا يشعرون﴾: (لا) is prohibitive; (تقتلوه): an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لا, the wāw is the fāʿil (agent), and the hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (عسى): a past verb among the verbs of hope (afʿāl al-rajāʾ), its noun is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "هو"; the interpreted maṣdar (maṣdar muʾawwal) from ﴿أن ينفعنا﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of عسى, accusative (manṣūb); (أو نتخذه): conjoined to ينفعنا; the hāʾ is the first mafʿūl bihi, and (ولدًا) the second mafʿūl bihi; (وهم): the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and ﴿هم﴾ is a mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause (لا يشعرون): khabar; and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of ﴿آل فرعون﴾.

muyesser-irab:10-10.t:
﴿وأصبح فؤاد أم موسى فارغا﴾: the wāw is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya); (أصبح): an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb; (فؤاد): its noun; (أم موسى): muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (فارغًا): its khabar (predicate); the clause ﴿وأصبح فؤاد...﴾ is resumptive, a clause with no grammatical position.
﴿إن كادت لتبدي به لولا أن ربطنا على قلبها لتكون من المؤمنين﴾: (إن) is lightened from the heavy (inna), inoperative (muhmala); (كادت): a past verb among the verbs of approximation (afʿāl al-muqāraba), its noun is latent (mustatir); the lām is the differentiating lām (al-lām al-fāriqa); the clause (تبدي): the khabar (predicate) of كاد; (به): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تبدي﴾; (لولا): a particle of non-occurrence due to occurrence (imtināʿ li-wujūd); (أن): maṣdariyya, and together with what it governs it is equivalent to a maṣdar (verbal noun) that is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar is omitted, i.e. "لولا ربطنا على قلبها حاصل"; (على قلبها): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿ربطنا﴾; the apodosis (jawāb) of لولا is omitted, i.e. "لأبدت به"; (لتكون): the lām is of causation (taʿlīl), and (تكون) is an incomplete imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām, and the interpreted maṣdar from أن and the verb is genitive (majrūr) by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿ربطنا﴾ as well; (من المؤمنين): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar of تكون.

muyesser-irab:11-11.t: ﴿وقالت لأخته قصيه فبصرت به عن جنب وهم لا يشعرون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; (قالت): a past verb, and a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent), its implied form being "هي", i.e. the mother of Moses; (لأخته): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿قالت﴾; (قصيه): an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, the yāʾ is the fāʿil, and the hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (فبصرت): the fāʾ is a conjunction joining to something omitted; (به): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿بصرت﴾; (عن جنب): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil of بصرت, i.e. "بصرت به مستخفية كائنة عن جنب", or of the pronoun in به, i.e. "بعيدًا"; the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), ﴿هم﴾ is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause (لا يشعرون): khabar (predicate).

muyesser-irab:12-12.t: ﴿وحرمنا عليه المراضع من قبل فقالت هل أدلكم على أهل بيت يكفلونه لكم وهم له ناصحون﴾: the wāw is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya); (حرمنا): verb and fāʿil (agent); (عليه): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿حرمنا﴾; (المراضع): mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause ﴿وحرمنا عليه المراضع﴾ is resumptive, a clause with no grammatical position; (من قبل): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), or attached to ﴿حرمنا﴾; (فقالت): the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (implying an omitted clause); (هل): an interrogative particle; (أدلكم): an imperfect verb, the fāʿil is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "أنا", and the kāf is the mafʿūl bihi; (على أهل بيت): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿أدلكم﴾; the clause (يكفلونه): a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿أهل بيت﴾; (لكم): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿يكفلونه﴾; the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), ﴿هم﴾ is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and ﴿له﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿ناصحون﴾; (ناصحون): khabar (predicate).

muyesser-irab:13-13.t:
﴿فرددناه إلى أمه كي تقر عينها ولا تحزن﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; (رددناه): verb, fāʿil (agent) and mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (إلى أمه): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿رددناه﴾; (كي): a maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle; (تقر): an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by ﴿كي﴾, and the interpreted maṣdar (maṣdar muʾawwal) from كي and the verb is in the position of genitive by the omitted lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿رددناه﴾; (ولا تحزن): conjoined to تقر.
﴿ولتعلم أن وعد الله حق ولكن أكثرهم لا يعلمون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, the lām is of causation (taʿlīl), and (تعلم): an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām; أن and what follows it stand in place of the two objects of تعلم; (أن) is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), (وعد) is its noun, and (حق): its khabar (predicate); the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); (ولكن أكثرهم): لكن is an abrogating particle, (أكثر) is its noun, and ﴿هم﴾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause (لا يعلمون): its khabar.

muyesser-irab:14-14.t: ﴿ولما بلغ أشده واستوى آتيناه حكما وعلما وكذلك نجزي المحسنين﴾: the wāw is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya); (لما): temporal (ḥīniyya, "when"), or linking (rābiṭa); (بلغ): a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "هو"; (أشده): mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (استوى): conjoined to بلغ; the clause (آتيناه) has no grammatical position, because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition (jawāb sharṭ ghayr jāzim); (آتيناه): a past verb, fāʿil and first mafʿūl bihi; (حكمًا): second mafʿūl bihi; (علمًا): conjoined to ﴿حكمًا﴾; the clause ﴿ولما بلغ...﴾ is resumptive, a clause with no grammatical position; ﴿كذلك﴾: the kāf is a noun meaning "like" (mithl), indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun) placed before its governor, i.e. "وجزاءً مثلَ ذلك نجزي المحسنين"; (ذلك): ﴿ذا﴾ is a demonstrative in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), the lām is for distance, and the kāf is a particle of address; ﴿نجزي﴾ is an imperfect verb, the fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "نحن", and ﴿المحسنين﴾ is mafʿūl bihi.

muyesser-irab:15-15.t:
﴿ودخل المدينة على حين غفلة من أهلها﴾: ﴿ودخل المدينة﴾: conjoined to something omitted; (دخل المدينة): verb, latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent), and an object by extension (ʿalā al-saʿa); (على حين غفلة): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of المدينة, or of the fāʿil of دخل, i.e. "مختلسًا" (stealthily); (من أهلها): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of غفلة.
﴿فوجد فيها رجلين يقتتلان هذا من شيعته وهذا من عدوه﴾: (فوجد): conjoined to دخل; (فيها): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿وجد﴾; (رجلين): mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause (يقتتلان): a naʿt of رجلين; (هذا): mubtadaʾ (subject); (من شيعته): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar (predicate), and the clause is a second naʿt of رجلين, and it has been said a ḥāl; ﴿وهذا من عدوه﴾: conjoined to it.
﴿فاستغاثه الذي من شيعته على الذي من عدوه﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; (استغاثه): a past verb and mafʿūl bihi; (الذي): fāʿil; (من شيعته): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause), and the ṣila clause has no grammatical position.
﴿فوكزه موسى فقضى عليه قال هذا من عمل الشيطان إنه عدو مضل مبين﴾: (فوكزه): likewise conjoined; (موسى): fāʿil (agent); (فقضى عليه): conjoined to فوكزه; (قال): a past verb, and the clause is resumptive, a clause with no grammatical position; (هذا): mubtadaʾ (subject); (من عمل الشيطان): khabar (predicate), and the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); the clause (إنه عدو): causal (taʿlīl); (إن) is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), the hāʾ is its noun, and (عدو) is its khabar; (مضل): naʿt (adjective); (مبين): a second naʿt.

muyesser-irab:17-17.t: ﴿قال رب بما أنعمت علي فلن أكون ظهيرا للمجرمين﴾: (بما): the bāʾ is a particle of oath and genitive, and the apodosis of the oath (jawāb al-qasam) is omitted, its implied form being "أقسم بإنعامك علي بالمغفرة لأتوبن"; ﴿ما﴾ is maṣdariyya, and the interpreted maṣdar (maṣdar muʾawwal) is genitive (majrūr) by the bāʾ of the oath; the fāʾ conjoins to the omitted apodosis; (لن): a particle of negation, accusative-governing and future; (أكون): an incomplete (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, its noun is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "أنا"; (ظهيرًا): its khabar; (للمجرمين): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿ظهيرًا﴾; and it has been said: the bāʾ and what it governs are attached to an implied ﴿اعصمني﴾, and the fāʾ in ﴿فلن أكون﴾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, because it is the apodosis of an implied condition.

muyesser-irab:16-16.t: ﴿قال رب إني ظلمت نفسي فاغفر لي فغفر له إنه هو الغفور الرحيم﴾: ﴿رب﴾: the one addressed (munādā), annexed to the omitted yāʾ of the first person; (إن) is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), the yāʾ is its noun, and the clause ﴿ظلمت نفسي﴾: the khabar (predicate) of إن; (فاغفر لي): the fāʾ is a conjunction, (اغفر) is a verb of supplication, and (لي): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿اغفر﴾; (فغفر له): conjoined; (إن) is an abrogating particle, the hāʾ is its noun, ﴿هو﴾: a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl), (الغفور): khabar, and (الرحيم): a second khabar; or ﴿هو﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject), and (الغفور الرحيم): two khabars of it, and the clause is the khabar of إن.

muyesser-irab:18-18.t:
﴿فأصبح في المدينة خائفا يترقب﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; (أصبح): an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb, its noun is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "هو"; (في المدينة): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); (خائفًا): the khabar (predicate) of أصبح; or (في المدينة): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar of أصبح, and (خائفًا): ḥāl; or the verb ﴿أصبح﴾ is complete (tāmm) and its fāʿil (agent) is latent, (في المدينة) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to it, and (خائفًا) is a ḥāl; the clause (يترقب): a second ḥāl, or a second khabar, or a ḥāl of the pronoun in ﴿خائفًا﴾; the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of يترقب is omitted, i.e. "يترقب المكروه" (awaiting what is dreaded).
﴿فإذا الذي استنصره بالأمس يستصرخه﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; (إذا): of surprise (fujāʾiyya); (الذي): mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause (استنصره): the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, a clause with no grammatical position; (بالأمس): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿استنصر﴾; the clause (يستصرخه): the khabar of الذي; and what يستصرخه is attached to is omitted, i.e. "على قبطي آخر" (against another Copt).
﴿قال له موسى إنك لغوي مبين﴾: (قال): a past verb; ﴿له﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to it; (موسى): fāʿil; (إنك): (إن) is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), the kāf is its noun, the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and (غوي مبين): two khabars of ﴿إن﴾.

muyesser-irab:19-19.t:
﴿فلما أن أراد أن يبطش بالذي هو عدو لهما﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; (لما): temporal (ḥīniyya), or linking (rābiṭa); (أن): connective (ṣila, i.e. redundant); (أراد): a past verb; أن and what follows it are equivalent to a maṣdar (verbal noun) that is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of أراد; (بالذي): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يبطش﴾; ﴿هو﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject); (عدو): khabar (predicate); (لهما): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective); the clause ﴿هو عدو لهما﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذي, a clause with no grammatical position.
﴿قال يا موسى أتريد أن تقتلني كما قتلت نفسا بالأمس﴾: (قال): a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); (أتريد): the hamza is for interrogation, (تريد) is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and أن and what lies within its scope are the mafʿūl bihi of تريد; ﴿كما﴾: the kāf is a noun meaning "like" (mithl), indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of accusative as a naʿt of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), and ﴿ما﴾ is maṣdariyya, interpreted together with what follows it as a maṣdar that is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), the implied form being "تقتلني قتلا مثلَ قتلك نفسًا بالأمس"; ﴿قتلت﴾ is verb and fāʿil, (نفسًا) mafʿūl bihi; (بالأمس): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿قتلت﴾; the clause ﴿قتلت﴾ is the ṣila of the particle relative ﴿ما﴾, a clause with no grammatical position.
﴿إن تريد إلا أن تكون جبارا في الأرض وما تريد أن تكون من المصلحين﴾: (إن) is negating; (تريد): an imperfect verb, nominative, its fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "أنت"; (إلا): a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); أن and what follows it are equivalent to a maṣdar that is the mafʿūl bihi of تريد; (جبارًا): the khabar of تكون; (في الأرض): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted naʿt of ﴿جبارًا﴾; (ما) is negating; (تريد): an imperfect verb, nominative, its fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "أنت"; أن and what follows it are equivalent to a maṣdar that is the mafʿūl bihi of تريد; ﴿من المصلحين﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar of تكون.

muyesser-irab:20-20.t:
﴿وجاء رجل من أقصى المدينة يسعى﴾: the wāw is a conjunction joining to something omitted; (جاء رجل): verb and fāʿil (agent); (من أقصى المدينة): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted naʿt (adjective) of رجل, and the clause (يسعى): a second naʿt, or a ḥāl (circumstantial); or (من أقصى المدينة): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿جاء﴾, and the clause (يسعى): a naʿt only.
﴿قال يا موسى إن الملأ يأتمرون بك ليقتلوك فاخرج إني لك من الناصحين﴾: (إن الملأ): (إن) is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), (الملأ) is its noun, and the clause (يأتمرون): the khabar (predicate) of إن; (بك): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿يأتمرون﴾; (ليقتلوك): the lām is of causation (taʿlīliyya), and (يقتلوك) is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after it, and the interpreted maṣdar (maṣdar muʾawwal) from أن and the verb is genitive (majrūr) by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿يأتمرون﴾; (فاخرج): the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (implying an omitted clause), i.e. "إن سمعت نصيحتي فاخرج" (if you heed my advice, then leave); (إني): (إن) is an abrogating particle and the yāʾ is its noun; (لك): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl, and it has been said: attached to ﴿الناصحين﴾; ﴿من الناصحين﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar of إن.

muyesser-irab:21-21.t: ﴿فخرج منها خائفا يترقب قال رب نجني من القوم الظالمين﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction joining to something omitted; (منها): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿خرج﴾; (خائفًا): ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause (يترقب): a second ḥāl, and the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of يترقب is omitted, i.e. "الشر" (harm), or their catching up with him, and it has been said: he awaited Allah's rescue; (رب): the one addressed (munādā); (نجني): a verb of supplication, and the yāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi; (من القوم): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿نجني﴾; (الظالمين): naʿt (adjective).

muyesser-irab:22-22.t: ﴿ولما توجه تلقاء مدين قال عسى ربي أن يهديني سواء السبيل﴾: the wāw is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya); (لما) is an adverb meaning "when" (ḥīna) containing the sense of condition; (توجه): a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "هو"; (تلقاء مدين): an adverb of place (ẓarf makān) attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿توجه﴾; (مدين): muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), made a diptote (mamnūʿ min al-ṣarf) for being a proper name and feminine; the clause ﴿قال...﴾ has no grammatical position, because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition (jawāb sharṭ ghayr jāzim); (عسى): an inflexible (jāmid) past verb among the verbs of hope (afʿāl al-rajāʾ); (ربي): its noun; أن and what lies within its scope are its khabar (predicate); (سواء السبيل): a second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), or accusative by removal of the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ); the clause ﴿ولما توجه...﴾ is resumptive, a clause with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:23-23.t:
﴿ولما ورد ماء مدين وجد عليه أمة من الناس يسقون﴾: (وجد): a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "هو"; (عليه): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿وجد﴾; (أمة): mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (من الناس): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of أمة; the clause (يسقون): a second naʿt, or a ḥāl (circumstantial); and the mafʿūl bihi of يسقون is omitted since it is known, i.e. "مواشيهم" (their livestock).
﴿ووجد من دونهم امرأتين تذودان﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; (وجد): conjoined to the first وجد; (من دونهم): a preposition and its genitive noun likewise attached to ﴿وجد﴾; (امرأتين): first mafʿūl bihi; the clause (تذودان): a naʿt of امرأتين. [Translator's note: so in the source, "first mafʿūl bihi", although no second object is named.]
﴿قال ما خطبكما قالتا لا نسقي حتى يصدر الرعاء وأبونا شيخ كبير﴾: ﴿ما﴾ is an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); (خطبكما): khabar (predicate), and the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); (قالتا): a past verb, the tāʾ is the quiescent tāʾ of the feminine, given a fatḥa to suit the alif of the dual, and the alif is the fāʿil; the clause (لا نسقي): the object of their saying; (حتى): a particle of limit (ghāya) and genitive; (يصدر): an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after حتى, and the interpreted maṣdar (maṣdar muʾawwal) from أن and the verb is genitive (majrūr) by حتى, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿نسقي﴾; (الرعاء): fāʿil; the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); (أبونا): mubtadaʾ; (شيخ): khabar; (كبير): naʿt.

muyesser-irab:24-24.t:
﴿فسقى لهما ثم تولى إلى الظل﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction joining to something omitted and implied; (سقى): a past verb; (لهما): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿سقى﴾; the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) is omitted, i.e. "غنمهما لأجلهما" (their sheep, for their sake); (ثم): a conjunction; (تولى): a past verb; (إلى الظل): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿تولى﴾.
﴿فقال رب إني لما أنزلت إلي من خير فقير﴾: (رب): the one addressed (munādā); (إن) is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and the yāʾ is its noun; (لما): the lām is a preposition, and (ما) is an indefinite noun meaning "thing", or a relative noun, i.e. "for whatever thing", or "for that which You sent down"; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿فقير﴾; (أنزلت): verb and fāʿil (agent); the clause ﴿أنزلت﴾ is a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿ما﴾, or the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, a clause with no grammatical position; (إلي): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿أنزلت﴾; (من خير): ḥāl (circumstantial); (فقير): the khabar (predicate) of إن.

muyesser-irab:25-25.t:
﴿فجاءته إحداهما تمشي على استحياء﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction joining to something omitted; (إحداهما): fāʿil (agent); the clause (تمشي): a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil; (على استحياء): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl of the fāʿil latent in تمشي, i.e. "مستحيية" (bashfully).
﴿قالت إن أبي يدعوك ليجزيك أجر ما سقيت لنا﴾: (إن) is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), (أبي) is its noun, and the clause (يدعوك): its khabar (predicate); (ليجزيك): the lām is of causation (taʿlīl), (يجزيك): an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām of causation, and the interpreted maṣdar (maṣdar muʾawwal) from أن and the verb is genitive (majrūr) by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿يدعوك﴾; the kāf is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (أجر): second mafʿūl bihi; ﴿ما﴾ is maṣdariyya, and it with what follows is equivalent to a maṣdar that is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), i.e. "أجر سقايتك" (the wage of your watering); (لنا): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿سقيت﴾.
﴿فلما جاءه وقص عليه القصص قال لا تخف نجوت من القوم الظالمين﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction joining to something omitted; (قص): a past verb; (عليه): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿قص﴾; (القصص): mafʿūl bihi; the clause (قال): has no grammatical position; (لا) is prohibitive; (تخف): an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لا; (نجوت): verb and fāʿil (agent); (من القوم): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿نجوت﴾; ﴿الظالمين﴾ is a naʿt (adjective).

muyesser-irab:26-26.t:
